messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: GeoDNS probe failures detected for us-midwest (az-usw-2) region. 45% of probes returning NXDOMAIN or SERVFAIL against our CF resolver pool in the past 3m. Pager sent to oncall. https://monitoring.internal/alert/5632109876 :rotating_light:

olivia (oncall): On it. Confirming scope — are customers actually seeing 5xx or just probe noise?

raj (sre): Seeing increased 5xx for inbound API on us-midwest edge — correlates with DNS errors. Quick sanity dig: `dig +short NS api.redwood-inference.internal @1.1.1.1` returns inconsistent sets from different resolvers.

maria (netops): Looks like Cloudflare responder nodes in that metro are returning NXDOMAIN for some record subsets. Route53 health checks look green from our control plane though. Could be propagation/skew.

alice (eng): Customer report from acme-inc: intermittent failures for webhook deliveries (~15% loss) since ~09:12 UTC. They retried, some succeeded after 30s.

olivia (oncall): Triage plan: 1) confirm impact + scope 2) apply temporary routing fallback for API traffic away from us-midwest 3) open ticket with Cloudflare & AWS 4) handoff if not resolved in 1h. Raj, can you start failover?

raj (sre): Starting now — shifting geodns fallback policy to prefer us-east for api.redwood-inference.internal by lowering weight for us-midwest and increasing us-east. Applying change via our geodns control plane. Command snippet: ```
# CLI
redwood-geodns update weights --record api.redwood-inference.internal \
  --weights us-midwest=10 us-east=90 --reason "regional resolver anomalies"
```

maria (netops): Reconfig applied, TTL for the record is 30s so should propagate quickly. Pushing a proxy-level route override too to drain new connections from us-midwest.

incident-bot: ACTION: route change deployed by raj at 5632109955. Auto-check in 2m.

olivia (oncall): Noting customer impact: ~12% increase in p50 latency for API tokens routed through us-midwest prior to change, spike in retries visible. Marking SEV-2 for now until we confirm full customer-visible mitigation.

raj (sre): Post-failover metrics show successful drop in errors to ~2% after 90s. Inflight retries are completing. Rolling window 5m error rate down from 18% to 3% for the affected domain.

maria (netops): Reaching out to Cloudflare support — opened ticket CF-89231 with trace logs and example resolver IPs returning NXDOMAIN. Cloud-support-bot replied with next steps (collect pcaps, which we are doing).

cloud-support-bot: Cloudflare ticket CF-89231 acknowledged. Please provide `dig +trace` output from affected edge and probe IPs and any sample query IDs. ETA initial response 20-30m.

alice (eng): Pushing an internal customer note to status page drafts: "We detected intermittent DNS resolution issues affecting a subset of traffic in the US-Midwest region. We implemented an automated regional fallback to route traffic to nearby healthy regions. Some customers may have experienced transient failures; requests are now routing successfully. Investigating root cause with Cloudflare and AWS."

olivia (oncall): Good. I'll escalate to oncall manager in 15 if Cloudflare doesn't have actionable response. Also paging platform-sre to watch for egde-cache thrash in us-east due to sudden traffic shift. @raj @maria please monitor.

raj (sre): Watching for cache miss storms. So far CPU on east pool up ~8%, no saturation. We'll enable burst autoscale policy if CPU > 70% for 2min.

maria (netops): Cloudflare ticket now shows an internal note: potential unhealthy resolver pool in us-midwest; they are running diagnostics and will share results. Meanwhile they suggest keeping our fallback in place.

incident-bot: NOTE: On-call handoff scheduled at 5632112000 UTC. Current oncall: olivia. Next: sam (oncall-next).

olivia (oncall): If the Cloudflare diagnosis points to transient node-level issue, we'll keep the fallback for 30min after clear to allow caches to warm and avoid oscillation. After that we'll step traffic back gradually with canary weights.

alice (eng): Quick sanity command examples sent to Cloudflare support: ```
# sample dig from affected probe
dig +short @{resolver_ip} api.redwood-inference.internal A
# tcpdump suggestion
sudo tcpdump -w cf-debug.pcap host {resolver_ip} and port 53
```

raj (sre): Adding post-incident todo: - add higher-fidelity resolver health checks (per-record) - make fallback weight change atomic with flapping protection - add alert to detect rapid NXDOMAIN surge for top-level service records

maria (netops): Cloudflare now reporting degraded resolver process on a subset of nodes, mitigation in progress. They will post final root cause when fixed.

olivia (oncall): Current status: Traffic rerouted, customer errors largely mitigated, Cloudflare investigating. Keeping SEV-2 open until we get root cause + plan. Preparing to handoff to sam at shift change — leaving notes in the incident doc and linking Cloudflare ticket and our geodns change id: geodns-change-7890.

incident-bot: UPDATE: SEV-2 still active. Escalation log updated.

olivia (oncall): Thanks team — please add anything to the incident thread if you see regression. I'll create the postmortem draft after root cause confirmed. :white_check_mark:
